title: Latency-aware, economics-driven scaling policy for dedicated fleets
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy engine variant for Dedicated fleets that fuses latency signals with token-economics to make safe, cost-aware scale decisions. The goal is to deliver throughput guarantees without unbounded cost by: 1) computing a composite target metric that blends tokens/sec, p95 latency, and KV cache hit rate; 2) using an economic penalty term (cost per token vs committed spend) to bias scaling toward cheaper model variants or quantized replicas when appropriate; 3) bounding actuation with slew-rate limits, reservoir bursting credits, and integrity fences that prevent oscillation; 4) exposing simulation and dry-run modes so operators can validate policies against historical traces and incident windows. This ticket covers the policy DSL, metric fusion library, controller integration, simulator scenarios, and Console observability surface for decision reasons.
acceptance_criteria: New policy can declare composite targets combining token_rate, p95_latency, and kv_hit_rate with configurable weights
Controller produces a scale intent every 10s and applies a default slew limit of +20% capacity per minute unless overridden
Economic penalty function is pluggable and can trigger downgrade to lower-cost model variant or enable quantized replicas when committed spend threshold is nearing
Safety leash prevents scaling above max_committed_capacity and caps burst consumption to a replenishing credit reservoir
Simulator reproduces at least two historical incidents from the last 12 months and shows expected headroom and cost delta compared to current autoscaler
Decision reasoning (inputs, intermediate scores, chosen action) is logged to Console for every scaling action and available via API
Automated integration tests cover policy evaluation, reservoir accounting, and rollback behavior under fluctuating synthetic load
tasks: Write design doc and policy DSL proposal (link in updates)
Implement metric fusion library in autoscaler core with unit tests
Add economic penalty module and model-variant selection hooks
Integrate slew/credit safety leash into actuator path
Build simulator scenarios and dry-run harness using historical traces
Add decision-reason telemetry to Console and retention dashboard
Create regression/integration tests and CI job
Run chaos/load test on staging dedicated fleet and iterate
decisions: Metric fusion will use weighted z-score normalization to combine heterogeneous signals (chosen 2026-02-25)
Default control loop frequency set to 10s to balance responsiveness and signal stability (agreed 2026-02-27)
Economic penalty uses a sliding window cost burn rate vs committed monthly spend with linear penalty curve above 80% utilization (initial value chosen but tunable)
Safety leash design: dual limits (absolute max_committed_capacity and replenishable burst_credit reservoir) to support short spikes without long-term cost exposure

notes: This ticket intentionally separates economic decisioning from pure latency-driven scaling to allow future ML-based policy components to plug in without changing base safety constraints.
We must avoid coupling to a single model catalog implementation; plugin hooks will call a model-ranking service returning compatible variants and cost estimates.
Console UX should surface: composite score, contributing signals, chosen action, and 'why not scaled further' text derived from safety leash evaluation
